summary: Reviewed BookmarkSettingsViewModel.cs. The guard (!IsCreateMode || _ffmpegRunner is null || string.IsNullOrEmpty(_videoPath)) is De Morgan-equivalent to !CanNudge and satisfies compiler flow analysis — correct pattern. The InitializeAsync frame-capture block is structurally identical to NudgeAsync: IsBusy toggle, Guid-named temp file, ExtractFrameAsync with ConfigureAwait(true), Bitmap swap with disposal, catch-LogWarning, finally with IsBusy=false and best-effort temp cleanup. All AC confirmed. One medium-priority improvement flagged: the capture block is duplicated in two places; a private CaptureFrameAsync helper would reduce the maintenance surface (not blocking). No architectural or correctness issues found.

comments.note: The ~20-line frame-capture block (IsBusy toggle, tempPath gen, ExtractFrameAsync, Bitmap swap, catch-LogWarning, finally-cleanup) is duplicated between InitializeAsync and NudgeAsync. The only difference is the log message string. Extracting this to a private CaptureFrameAsync(string videoPath, long positionMs, string context) helper would reduce the maintenance surface — any future changes to the capture pattern (e.g., format change, additional cleanup) would only need to happen once. Not blocking, but worth addressing in a follow-up WP.

Guard logic confirmed: `!IsCreateMode || _ffmpegRunner is null || string.IsNullOrEmpty(_videoPath)` is De Morgan-equivalent to `!CanNudge`. Using the expanded form instead of `!CanNudge` is intentional — it satisfies the compiler's flow analysis for the subsequent null-safe dereferences of _ffmpegRunner and _videoPath without requiring null-forgiving operators. This is the correct approach.

NudgeAsync has an IsBusy guard at entry (`if (IsBusy) return;`) to prevent concurrent nudge captures. InitializeAsync has no such guard, which is correct — InitializeAsync is called exactly once before the dialog is shown (enforced by AvaloniaBookmarkSettingsService), so concurrent access is not possible.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md entry for BookmarkSettingsViewModel.InitializeAsync should be updated to note that it now performs an initial frame capture when CanNudge is true, and that failures are swallowed as warnings (non-fatal). This distinguishes its error contract from a typical initialize method.
